died: 749 (per task brief; Wikipedia snippet gives 4 Dec 749)
language: Greek (with Latin in Migne's facing column)
role_place: Monk and priest at Mar Saba near Jerusalem; earlier in the Umayyad administration at Damascus (per task brief and the Vita read in PG 94).
why_relevant: Earliest Greek Christian chapter on Islam (De haeresibus, c. 101: 'heresy of the Ishmaelites') and the Dialogue/Disputatio with a Saracen (PG 94 cols 1585-1597).
fame: Doctor of the Church and iconodule theologian; the Ishmaelite chapter is the part of De haeresibus that most attracted scholarly attention (Pearse 2026 blog, which I read). Scholarly citation counts not checked.

born: c. 672/673 (per task brief and the Latin Library index page 'VENERABILIS BEDA PRESBYTER (672/3 - 735 A.D.)')
role_place: Monk and priest at Wearmouth-Jarrow, Northumbria; historian, exegete and chronographer.
why_relevant: Brief Saracen notices in the Historia ecclesiastica (5.23, AD 729 annal), in his Genesis commentary (Ishmael, Gen 16:12) and in De temporum ratione; he gives no sustained doctrinal critique of Islam in the works I checked.
fame: Very well known as the 'Father of English history' and for the Historia ecclesiastica; the Saracen passages are minor and rarely quoted (I found no citing literature in my searches).
